label: Right Triangle Trigonometry
overview: Trigonometry lets you find unknown sides and angles in a right triangle using fixed ratios between the sides. Three ratios — sine, cosine, and tangent — each relate a chosen acute angle to two of the three sides. Every SAT right-triangle trig question gives you two of those three quantities and asks for the third. The whole skill reduces to: pick the right ratio, write one equation, solve.

workedExamples.problem: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is 13 and one acute angle is 22.6°. Find the side opposite that angle.

steps.title: Label the sides
steps.content: Relative to the 22.6° angle: the hypotenuse is 13, and the opposite side is what we want. Sine connects opposite and hypotenuse.

steps.title: Substitute and solve
steps.content: Plug in the known angle and hypotenuse, then multiply both sides by 13.

workedExamples.problem: A ramp rises 4 feet vertically over a horizontal run of 10 feet. What is the angle of elevation?

steps.title: Identify the sides relative to the unknown angle
steps.content: The vertical rise (4 ft) is opposite the angle of elevation. The horizontal run (10 ft) is adjacent. No hypotenuse needed — use tangent.

steps.title: Apply inverse tangent
steps.content: Use tan⁻¹ to recover the angle from the ratio.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using cosine instead of sine (or vice versa)
commonMistakes.fix: Sine uses opposite and hypotenuse. Cosine uses adjacent and hypotenuse. Sketch and label the triangle first — the right ratio picks itself.
Opposite never touches the reference angle. Adjacent touches the reference angle but is not the hypotenuse. Relabel every time you switch reference angles.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting to use inverse trig when solving for an angle
commonMistakes.fix: If the unknown is θ, apply sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, or tan⁻¹ to the ratio. Writing sin(θ) = 0.574 and leaving it there is not a solved answer.

quickTip: Label hyp, opp, adj on the triangle before you pick a ratio — the correct ratio is the one that uses exactly the two sides you have or want.
